evidence: unreadable: In seg1:start and seg1:mid the 'Ukraine 22' tag on the rack is tiny and sits among coloured cables, so it is illegible on a phone. The small grey '2016' ghost mark (seg0:mid) is also hard to read.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: seg2:start to seg2:end: the shutters on GROCER, PHONES and CAFE close while Data stands beside them pointing. '$9.1 billion' appears only as a headline (seg2:end), and three shops shutting gives no sense of how big that sum is.
weakest_scene.root_cause: Data is placed next to the shutters, not gripping them, and the picture has no unit that turns $9.1B into something you can see at a glance. It reads as 'shops closed', not 'nine billion lost'.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Have Data grab and pull each shutter down with both hands (a grip act on the shutter handles). Put the scale on the street itself, e.g. a long row of shops going dark into the distance, or a till readout draining, so the size of $9.1B reads without the label.
